rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause answers 9:67 and identifies the people who receive pardon as those attached to the believers; its sentence continues the linked sequence of clauses.
rows.anchor: هذه تقابل قوله : { المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض } ( التوبة : 67 ) لبيان أن الطائفة التي ينالها العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers share the bond of Islamic allegiance as equals; its sense conveys sincerity and mutual support, unlike hypocrites who seem to arise from one another in vices.
rows.anchor: اللحمة الجامعة بينهم هي ولاية الإسلام ، فهم فيها على السواء ليس واحد منهم مقلدا للآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added description of believers as establishing prayer honors prayer as the greatest form of enjoining what is right.
rows.anchor: بأن الصلاة هي أعظم المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving alms by believers contrasts with the hypocrites' withholding their hands.
rows.anchor: ويؤتون الزكاة } مقابل قوله في المنافقين { ويقبضون أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God and His Messenger contrasts with the hypocrites' forgetting God, since obedience entails attentiveness to the one obeyed.
rows.anchor: لأن الطاعة تقتضي مراقبة المطاع فهي ضد النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God will show mercy to believers counters the statement that He forgot the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: سيرحمهم الله } مقابل قوله في المنافقين { فنسيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle reinforces the certainty of coming mercy; with a present verb it conveys what قد conveys with a past verb, as in 93:5.
rows.anchor: والسين لتأكيد حصول الرحمة في المستقبل ، فحرف الاستقبال يفيد مع المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative signals that the people described are worthy of what follows because of the qualities listed before it.
rows.anchor: صاروا أحرياء به من أجلل الأوصاف المذكورة قبل اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might enables Him to benefit His allies, and His wisdom places reward with those who deserve it; this explains His mercy.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى لعزته ينفع أولياءه وأنه لحكمته يضع الجزاء لمستحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' reward follows their mutual allegiance as the promise to hypocrites follows their mutual affiliation; it also explains the promised mercy, like 9:21.
rows.anchor: وهي أيضا كالاستئناف البياني الناشىء عن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the past-tense promise is that it recalls a promise already made in Quranic verses so as to affirm its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: إما لأنه إخبار عن وعد تقدم في آي القرآن قصد من الإخبار به التذكير به لتحقيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the promise is put in past tense like a contract formula, signaling a binding commitment that cannot fail; 9:68 uses the same form.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يكون قد صيغ هذا الوعد بلفظ المضي على طريقة صيغ العقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the believers instead of using a pronoun fixes their identity in the hearer's mind and strengthens the verb's attachment to them.
rows.anchor: لتقريرهم في ذهن السامع ليتمكن تعلق الفعل بهم فضل تمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur refers readers to his earlier discussion of the description of gardens with rivers flowing beneath them at 2:25.
rows.anchor: عند قوله تعالى : { وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added dwellings mean palaces and good homes in the gardens, free of filth and traces of cooking, like the purified spouses of 2:25.
rows.anchor: أي ليس فيها شيء من خبث المساكن من الأوساخ وآثار علاج الطبخ ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn means lasting residence and continuous settlement; the gardens of Eden are the same gardens already mentioned.
rows.anchor: الخلد والاستقرار المستمر ، فجنات عدن هي الجنات المذكورة قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated name varies the expression and honors the gardens; this is why the text does not say simply that the dwellings are in them.
rows.anchor: فذكرها بهذا اللفظ من الإظهار في مقام الإضمار مع التفنن في التعبير والتنويه بالجنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported occasion says the passage concerns the hypocrite Thalaba b. Hatib, who sought the Prophet's prayer for wealth, became rich, refused alms on his livestock, repented, but the Prophet refused his offering; the report says it remained unaccepted through the first three caliphs until Thalaba died under Uthman.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت في ثعلبة بن حاطب من المنافقين سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدعو له بسعة الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another attribution names Mu'attib b. Qushayr; on this account plural pronouns represent one person, with an individual's deed attached to his clan in Arab usage.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فضمائر الجمع في لنصدقن وما بعده مراد بها واحد وإنما نسبت الفعل إلى جماعة المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur also allows that Thalaba asked and some companions such as Mu'attib followed his example, received similar wealth, and became stingy, though no separate story about them is known.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن ثعلبة سأل ذلك فتبعه بعض أصحابه مثل معتب بن قشير فأوتي مثل ما أوتي ثعلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge to give alms explains the preceding covenant, and لنصدقن is assimilated from لنتصدقن for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لنصدقن } بيان لجملة { عاهد الله } وفعل { لنصدقن } أصله لنتصدقن فأدغم للتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away is from the covenant they made and from gratitude for their Lord's blessing.
rows.anchor: الإعراض : إعراضهم عن عهدهم وعن شكر نعمة ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أعقب means made something follow; because it is used with the sense of أعطى, it takes two objects, though its basic construction has a preposition.
rows.anchor: ولما ضمن أعقب معنى أعطى نصب مفعولين والأصل أعقبهم بنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implicit subject of أعقبهم may be their described behavior or the stinginess understood from the verb; attributing the consequence to either is figurative causation.
rows.anchor: للمذكور من أحوالهم ، أو للبخل المأخوذ من بخلوا ، فإسناد الإعقاب مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is the subject: their action caused hypocrisy to persist in their hearts until death as requital for their defiance.
rows.anchor: أو يعود إلى اسم الله تعالى في قوله { من عاهد الله } أي جعل فعلهم ذلك سببا في بقاء النفاق في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading entails that Thalaba or Mu'attib died unbelievers, which sits uneasily with both being counted Companions and Thalaba being a veteran of Badr; some say the men meant were namesakes.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي إلى أن ثعلبة أو معتبا مات على الكفر وأن حرصه على دفع صدقته رياء وتقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrisy may instead mean committing sins while Muslim, a usage present in the Prophet's time, as when Hanzala said he had become a hypocrite; the Prophet explained his mistaken perception without rejecting the term.
rows.anchor: وهو إطلاق موجود في عصر النبوءة كقول حنظلة بن الربيع للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form نفاقا suggests newly acquired hypocrisy; otherwise it would be puzzling to say that already-known hypocrites acquired hypocrisy only after this deed.
rows.anchor: تنكير { نفاقا } المفيد أنه نفاق جديد وإلا فقد ذكروا منافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because repentance requires repairing what can be repaired, this command follows the account of those who stayed behind: they missed both fighting and spending on the campaign, and their wealth can benefit Muslims.
rows.anchor: لما كان من شرط التوبة تدارك ما يمكن تداركه مما فات وكان التخلف عن الغزو مشتملا على أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great expenditure on Tabuk depleted funds reserved for Muslim needs, so taking some wealth from those who stayed behind repairs part of the loss.
rows.anchor: استنفد المال المعد لنوائب المسلمين ، فإذا أخذ من المخلفين شيء من المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the repentant confessors offered the wealth that had caused them to stay behind and asked the Prophet to accept it, purify them, and seek forgiveness; he initially said he had not been ordered to take it, but accepted after this verse came down.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن الذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم قالوا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه أموالنا التي بسببها تخلفنا عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in من أموالهم refers to another group of people who admitted their sins.
rows.anchor: فالضمير عائد على آخرين اعترفوا بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ of تطهرهم can be second person, following the command خذ, or third-person feminine, referring to the charity; either reading shows that charity purifies and sanctifies.
rows.anchor: تاء الغائبة عائدة إلى الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya is making something pure and abundant in good: purification removes sins, while sanctification adorns with virtues; cleansing precedes adornment, so the alms expiate sins and bring great reward.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى مقام التخلية عن السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praying for them means supplicating for them; the Prophet's prayer is supplication, whereas God's prayer is mercy.
rows.anchor: الدعاء لهم . وتقدم آنفا عند قوله تعالى : { وصلوات الرسول } ( التوبة : 99 )

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abi Awfa says that after this verse the Prophet would say on receiving someone's alms, Allah, bless the family of so-and-so; his prayer joined the meaning of blessing with the word for prayer.
rows.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن أبي أوفى يجمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه في هذا الشأن بين معنى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains the command to pray for them: the Prophet's supplication is a cause of calm, with سكن used metonymically for what produces tranquility.
rows.anchor: سكن لهم ، أي سبب سكن لهم ، أي خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan is what one settles and rests in; figuratively, it is psychological calm, since fear unsettles the mind and causes anxiety. The Quran also uses it for night, homes, and a spouse.
rows.anchor: أي يطمأن إليه ويرتاح به . وهو مشتق من السكون بالمعنى المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet's prayer makes their souls more inclined to righteous acts: sin brings hesitation, while obedience brings assurance and certainty.
rows.anchor: أو لأن دعاءه لهم يزيد نفوسهم صلاحا وسكونا إلى الصالحات لأن المعصية تردد واضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This closing statement suits the prayer command: hearing means answering supplication and hints that the Prophet's prayer is accepted; knowing hints that it brings great good and rectitude.
rows.anchor: ذكر العليم إيماء إلى أنه ما أمره بالدعاء لهم إلا لأن في دعائه لهم خيرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Asim through Abu Bakr, Abu Ja'far, and Yaqub read plural صلواتك; Hafs from Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read singular صلاتك. Both mean the Prophet's prayer generally: the definite plural explicitly includes its instances, while the singular implies them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people's reply answers Hud's call; the sentence begins without a conjunction because it is dialogue responding to his invitation.
rows.anchor: بجواب عن دعوته ، ولذلك جردت الجملة عن العاطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their opening address marks the importance of what follows and treats Hud as distant through heedlessness; it may also reproach and blame him, either figuratively or through literal and figurative address together.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى الاهتمام بما سيقولونه ، وأنه جدير بأن يتنبه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of proof is slander: Hud brought signs, as 11:59 indicates, although the Quran does not identify a particular sign; it may have been his prediction of exceptional abundance and uninterrupted fertility.
rows.anchor: بهتان لأنه أتاهم بمعجزات لقوله تعالى : { وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم }

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: An authentic hadith says every prophet was given signs like those through which people believed; Ibn Ashur cites it while discussing Hud's signs.
rows.anchor: إلا أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

words: وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They meant Hud's signs did not match their demands; they present that as a reason for keeping their gods, but not as a logical inference from having seen no sign.
rows.anchor: وإنما أرادوا أن البينات التي جاءهم بها هود عليه السلام لم تكن طبقا لمقترحاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عن indicates departure: they will not leave their gods by reason of Hud's words, making his speech the proposed cause for abandoning them.
rows.anchor: لا نتركها تركا صادرا عن قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that an idol afflicted Hud is an explanatory resumption: his rejection of their message naturally prompts the question of what they think his preaching is.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني لأن قولهم : { وما نحن لك بمؤمنين } من شأنه أن يثير للسامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They attribute Hud's harm to one idol as a threat, implying that their gods together could crush him.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا ذلك من فعل بعض الآلهة تهديدا للناس بأنه لو تصدى له جميع الآلهة لدكوه دكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اعتراء means descending upon or afflicting, and the bāʾ marks accompanying contact: an evil struck him.
rows.anchor: والاعتراء : النزول والإصابة . والباء للملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean their gods afflicted Hud with madness before he began rejecting their worship, for some other reason. This is incoherent sophistry: the gods supposedly provoked someone who then opposed them.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أنهم يعنون أن آلهتهم أصابته بمس من قبل أن يقوم بدعوة رفض عبادتها لسبب آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here القول means spoken utterance, a form that implies they actually believe what they say.
rows.anchor: وهو يقتضي اعتقادهم ما يقولونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to their rejection, denial of his signs, resolve to worship idols, and praise of their power, Hud calls God to witness that he conveyed the message and they stubbornly denied his signs.
rows.anchor: أجابهم هود عليه السلام بأنه يشهد الله عليهم أنه أبلغهم وأنهم كابروا وجحدوا آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أشهد الله is a performative act phrased as a report, as are utterances whose effect is not externally visible and familiar contract formulas.
rows.anchor: لأن كل إنشاء لا يظهر أثره في الخلق من شأنه أن يقع بصيغة الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud calls the people to witness that he disavows their partners, immediately countering their wrong claim; the insertion interrupts his next statement, which continues in 11:57.
rows.anchor: مبادرة بإنكار المنكر وإن كان ذلك قد أتوا به استطرادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He uses an imperative for their witnessing so that the performative sound of the declaration is not diluted by the flavor of reporting.
rows.anchor: لأنه أراد مزاجة إنشاء الإشهاد دون رائحة معنى الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them to witness makes his disavowal certain and irrevocable, as a matter he has imposed upon himself before witnesses.
rows.anchor: تحقيق ذلك وأنه لا يتردد على أمر جازم قد أوجبه المشهود عليه على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its relative clause elided: the sense is the things that they associate with God.
rows.anchor: العائد محذوف . والتقدير : مما يشركونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative phrase refers to the idols, as confirmed by the collective address to plot against Hud in the next clause.
rows.anchor: ضمير الجمع المؤكد في قوله : { فكيدوني جميعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His disavowal implies that the idols cannot harm him, so he challenges his people to plot; he addresses people, while including their idols in the challenge to meet their belief and complete their humiliation.
rows.anchor: فرع على البراءة جملة { فكيدوني جميعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to plot is permission used as a taunt that exposes both idols' and people's inability, as in 77:39; it refutes their claim in 11:54.
rows.anchor: كناية عن التعجيز بالنسبة للأصنام وبالنسبة لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks a rise in rhetorical rank: after challenging them to plot, Hud tells them not to delay, expressing utmost contempt and that they cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: ثم ارتقى في رتبة التعجيز والاحتقار فنهاهم عن التأخير بكيدهم إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance on God explains the challenge: Hud is confident the people cannot harm him because he trusts in God, an old religious principle.
rows.anchor: وهو التعجيز والاحتقار . يعني : أنه واثق بعجزهم عن كيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Lord of both Hud and his opponents grounds reliance in God's ownership of all of them and power to protect some from others' injustice.
rows.anchor: لأنه مالكهم جميعا يدفع ظلم بعضهم بعضا

words: مَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about every creature being held by its forelock may be an adjective of God's name or a circumstantial clause; either serves the same purpose as the lordship description.
rows.anchor: في محل صفة لاسم الجلالة ، أو حال منه ، والغرض منها مثل الغرض من صفة الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking means grasping; the forelock is the hair falling over the forehead, and grasping it pictures control like holding a person's head so he cannot escape.
rows.anchor: والأخذ : الإمساك . والناصية : ما انسدل على الجبهة من شعر الرأس

words: مَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image is figurative because many creatures lack forelocks; it means God governs all, especially humans, and as owner and conqueror cannot be escaped or overcome.
rows.anchor: ومن بديع هذا المثل أنه أشد اختصاصا بالنوع المقصود من بين عموم الدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على is a metaphor of elevation for steadfast moral establishment, comparable to the believers being upon guidance in 2:5.
rows.anchor: مستعارة للتمكن المعنوي ، وهو الاتصاف الراسخ الذي لا يتغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a metaphor for actions conforming to justice and wisdom; justice resembles straightness and evenness, as in 19:43.
rows.anchor: مستعار للفعل الجاري على مقتضى العدل والحكمة لأن العدل يشبه بالاستقامة والسواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains reliance: God merits trust because He acts justly and supports His messengers, so He does not hand one who trusts Him over to wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن ربي على صراط مستقيم } تعليل لجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur points to analogous material in the account of Hud in al-Araf and notes that Shuayb was discussed there earlier.
rows.anchor: تقدم الكلام على نظائر بعض هذه الآية في قصة هود في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of نجينا is omitted; ومن خزي يومئذ is coordinated with that omitted object, meaning that Salih and the believers were saved from annihilating punishment and its disgrace.
rows.anchor: متعلق { نجينا } محذوف . وعطف { ومن خزي يومئذ } على متعلق { نجينا } المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination adds one favor to another, rather than describing two rescues; this differs from the account of Hud, where rescue from severe punishment is distinct in 11:58.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود من العطف عطف منة على منة لا عطف إنجاء على إنجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin in يومئذ compensates for an omitted genitive, meaning the day when God's command came.
rows.anchor: وتنوين { يومئذ } تنوين عوض عن المضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disgrace is the humiliation of punishment, as discussed shortly before.
rows.anchor: والخزي : الذل ، وهو ذل العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about God's power is parenthetical and is reinforced by three emphatic devices to stress its importance.
rows.anchor: وقد أكد الخبر بثلاث مؤكدات للاهتمام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Thamud wrongdoers hints that their polytheism caused the punishment and warns Meccan polytheists that they too may suffer the same fate.
rows.anchor: للإيماء بالموصول إلى علة ترتب الحكم ، أي لظلمهم وهو ظلم الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry that struck Thamud means the thunderbolt.
rows.anchor: والصيحة : الصاعقة أصابتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that they had never lived there.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يقيموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use tanwin, treating Thamud as the ancestor's name; Hamza, Hafs from Asim, and Yaqub omit it, treating Thamud as the people or tribe. Both are established Arab treatments of tribal names derived from ancestors.
rows.anchor: على اعتبار ثمود اسم جد الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur refers to the earlier discussion of بعدا in Noah's story at 11:44.
rows.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على { بعدا } في قصة نوح { وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين } ( هود : 44 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening about Shuayb sent to Midian parallels the wording about Salih sent to Thamud in 11:61.
rows.anchor: نظير قوله : { وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا } ( هود : 61 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb's instruction covers repairing belief, correcting a widespread commercial wrong by not short-changing measures and weights, and avoiding corruption on earth; tawhid comes first as the basis of reform.
rows.anchor: صلاح الأعمال والتصرفات في العالم بأن لا يفسدوا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cheating in measure and weight is singled out between belief and general conduct because it was widespread enough that they forgot its ugliness; it combines theft and betrayal of trusting buyers.
rows.anchor: إقدامهم عليه كان فاشيا فيهم حتى نسوا ما فيه من قبح وفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of fraud is reinforced by the positive command to give full measure and weight in the following verse.
rows.anchor: فعززه بالأمر بضده وهو إيفاؤهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His seeing them in good means they are enjoying blessing; he presents himself as a witness to God's favor, for which they owe gratitude.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر رؤيته ذلك لأنها في معنى الشهادة عليهم بنعمة الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr can mean a good condition or wealth; Ibn Ashur prefers wealth here because their resources remove any need to cheat, make the practice indefensible, and support preserving the blessing.
rows.anchor: ويطلق على المال كقوله : { إن ترك خيرا } ( البقرة : 180 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning may concern punishment in this world or the afterlife; the wording leaves both open and warns against ingratitude for blessing and disobeying its giver.
rows.anchor: عذابا يحل بهم إما يوم القيامة وإما في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhit grammatically describes the day but figuratively means that its punishment will encompass them; the genitive phrase makes this clear.
rows.anchor: على وجه المجاز العقلي ، أي محيط عذابه ، والقرينة هي إضافة العذاب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their address is another sarcastic remark, sharpened by four emphases: إن, the oath lām, and the restrictive force of لأنت.
rows.anchor: وبصيغة القصر في جملة { لأنت الحليم الرشيد } فاشتملت على أربعة مؤكدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the added sarcasm, al-halim means intelligent or rational, while al-rashid means sound in managing money.
rows.anchor: زيادة في التهكم : ذو الحلم أي العقل ، والرشيد : الحسن التدبير في المال
